definitions.explanation: The act of applying fertilizer to soil or plants to promote growth.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}に{施肥|せひ}を{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: Fertilization is carried out in spring.

examples.japanese: {適切|てきせつ}な{施肥|せひ}が{作物|さくもつ}の{成長|せいちょう}を{促|うなが}す。
{過剰|かじょう}な{施肥|せひ}は{土壌|どじょう}の{質|しつ}を{悪化|あっか}させることがある。
examples.english: Excessive fertilization can degrade soil quality.

notes:
A technical term used in agriculture and gardening. Composed of {施|ほどこ}す (to apply, to give) and {肥|こえ} (fertilizer). This word is often encountered in farming manuals, gardening guides, and agricultural science.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {施肥|せひ}を{行|おこな}う — to apply fertilizer
- {施肥|せひ}{量|りょう} — amount of fertilizer applied
- {施肥|せひ}{時期|じき} — fertilizing season/timing
- {追|つい}{肥|ひ}する — to apply additional fertilizer (top-dressing)

RELATED WORDS:
- {肥料|ひりょう} — fertilizer (the substance itself)
- {元肥|もとごえ} — base fertilizer (applied before planting)
- {追肥|ついひ} — additional fertilizer (applied during growth)
